title: Lovelace v. Northeast Presbytery
disposition_detail: Item 1 was denied: Presbytery could decline to institute process after investigation found no strong presumption of guilt. Item 2 was sustained: Presbytery erred in ruling the related complaint out of order for non-membership. No remand or further directive was expressly ordered.
first_summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal to try four elders after investigating favoritism charges and its ruling that dissolution of her church deprived her of standing to pursue a related complaint. The SJC upheld the refusal to institute process but sustained the membership issue, reasoning that jurisdiction properly invoked while she was a communicant member survived a later change in status.
summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal, after investigation, to try four elders on favoritism charges and its ruling that her related complaint was out of order because dissolution of her church ended her PCA membership. The SJC denied the first item because BCO 31-2 permits declining process when investigation raises no strong presumption of guilt. It sustained the second: jurisdiction properly invoked while a communicant member is not lost through a later status change. No remand was expressly ordered.

sources.supports: Issues, operative judgment, adopted reasoning, jurisdictional rule, and treatment of membership-status question.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Title and SJC identity appear at lines 1–5; the operative judgment is lines 151–156 and was unanimously approved at line 222.
evidence_notes.dispute: The two complaints concerned refusal to institute process against four elders and an out-of-order ruling based on non-membership; lines 112–150, printed pp. 189–190.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Item 1 was denied under BCO 31-2 and Item 2 sustained; lines 151–180 and 182–213, printed pp. 190–192.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The effect of dissolution on current membership was deemed moot; lines 186–200. The later panel judgment at lines 224–242 was expressly not affirmed and is not the operative decision.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The SJC relied on Chappell v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery as precedent that later status changes do not defeat properly invoked jurisdiction; lines 209–213.

source_limits: The referenced Coffin dissent is not included. The source includes an unaffirmed panel judgment, which must not be confused with the unanimous full-SJC decision.

score_reasons.decision: States the denial of Item 1 and sustaining of Item 2 without importing the unaffirmed panel’s remand.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Gives the BCO 31-2 investigation rule and continuing-jurisdiction rationale.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between declining process after investigation and losing jurisdiction through later status change.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the operative full-SJC judgment from Presbytery’s reasoning and the unaffirmed panel judgment.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the mixed result and jurisdictional rule.

verification_notes: Rechecked lines 151–213 against the synopsis. The final summary clarifies that the SJC upheld only Presbytery’s authority to decline process after investigation, not a merits acquittal, and omits the remand ordered solely by the unaffirmed panel.
